triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix tier_2_employee_tax multiplied the section 3241 tier 2 percentage by the full compensation received, with no representation of the different contribution base that 3201(c) cross-references to section 3231(e)(2), so the encoded tax applied the rate to an unlimited base the statute does not use.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-07-13): 26 USC 3201(c) reads 'Cross reference For application of different contribution bases with respect to the taxes imposed by subsections (a) and (b), see section 3231(e)(2).' The fix is fail-closed: the executable Money rule is deleted and replaced by deferred_outputs for both 3201(a) and 3201(b) taxes blocked by us:statutes/26/3231/e/2#compensation_excess_excluded_before_hospital_insurance_carveout; the module now exports only the Rate rule tier_2_applicable_percentage (= applicable_percentage_for_section_3201_b), which is new coverage, not a defect. The existing 3201(a) deferral reason was also rewritten (previously blamed non-executable 3101 context, now the 3231(e)(2) base), and the summary/quoting and YAML indentation were reflowed mechanically. Kind could arguably be called amount_mismatch since the resulting tax amount is wrong, but the root cause is a source clause (the 3231(e)(2) base limitation) that the encoding never represented.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a mere fail-closed policy retreat, but the pre-fix encoding was genuinely wrong against the source: the removed rule computed a USD `tier_2_employee_tax` as `max(0, compensation_received_for_services_rendered_by_employee_for_calendar_year * applicable_percentage_for_section_3201_b)`, applying the section 3241 rate to an unbounded compensation input. Read through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-07-13), 3201(c) cross-references 3231(e)(2), and 3231(e)(2)(A)(i) states that "compensation" does not include remuneration paid after remuneration equal to the applicable base, with (B)(ii) supplying a distinct tier 2 base "[f]or purposes of ... the taxes imposed by sections 3201(b), 3211(b), and 3221(b)" — a limitation clause the encoding never represented, so the encoded tax overstated the statutory tax for any employee above the tier 2 base. The change is not mechanical (an executable Money output was removed and replaced by a Rate-only rule, with two new deferred_outputs and blocked_by edges), and it is not a new-coverage enhancement, because the module already claimed the tier 2 tax amount surface that the missing clause made wrong.
triage.verifier_notes: Kind tension a reviewer should weigh: the taxonomy's parenthetical for unrepresented_clause says "the fix adds it", and here the fix does not add the 3231(e)(2) base — it deletes the tier_2_employee_tax rule and defers it (fail-closed), which superficially matches untraceable_branch's "the fix removes or re-grounds it". I still chose unrepresented_clause because the formula itself was correctly grounded in 3201(b) ("tax equal to the percentage determined under section 3241 ... of the compensation received"); the only thing wrong was the absent cross-referenced base limitation, i.e. a missing clause, not an ungrounded branch. amount_mismatch does not fit: no numeric literal, rate, or threshold changed anywhere in the diff (the imported 3241(b) percentage and its import hash sha256:12b52ccf... are unchanged); the harness summary's phrase "wrong amount" refers to the amount surface, not a wrong constant. Corroborating evidence that the defect was real but latent: the pre-fix test statutes/26/3201.test.yaml asserted tier_2_employee_tax = 4900 on compensation of 100000, which is below the tier 2 applicable base, so the missing cap never surfaced in tests. Both pre and post carry the same effective_from '1990-01-01' and the same Person/Year scope, so no period, entity, or polarity kind is in play. Residual uncertainty (why 0.78, not higher): the commit is an encoder refresh whose deferral reason is boilerplate-adjacent, and one could argue the fix is an executability retreat rather than a meaning correction — but the retreat is justified by a limitation that the resolved source text does state.
